title: add-benchmark-lab-adaptive-batching-reporting-pipeline-v87
author: Ariana Chen
body:
Motivation: The benchmark lab has been collecting steady profiling data but lacks an adaptive workload runner that combines mixed-variant traffic with dynamic batching heuristics. This PR adds an adaptive batching runner, telemetry hooks for per-batch KPIs, and a reporting pipeline update (v87) to ingest and aggregate the new metrics. The primary goal is to enable workload-driven batching experiments that feed the Optimize recommendations engine and provide better baselines for Dedicated capacity sizing.

Summary of changes: added a new adaptive workload runner (adaptive_batch_runner.py) that simulates mixed traffic patterns and chooses batching windows based on observed latency/throughput; introduced per-batch telemetry (batch_size, queue_wait_ms, batch_latency_ms, model_variant); extended reporting pipeline v87 to parse and store the new fields; added unit and integration tests for the runner and pipeline; docs update and runbook for operators.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement adaptive batching runner and generator
- [x] Emit structured telemetry compatible with existing reporting schema
- [x] Add ETL step and reporting pipeline v87
- [x] Add unit/integration tests and CI coverage
- [x] Add docs and runbook entries
- [x] Validate with small canary deployment in perf-canary cluster

Testing and verification: Ran local unit tests (benchmark-lab/tests/test_adaptive_runner.py) and integration test that pushes synthetic traffic to perf-canary. Verified that reporting pipeline correctly indexes batch-level metrics in the reporting datastore and that results appear in the benchmark lab dashboard. CI summary below shows a transient e2e flake that was rerun.

Rollout plan: merge to main, deploy reporting pipeline v87 to the staging reporting cluster, run 48-hour collector job with existing workloads and the new adaptive runner. If metrics remain stable, promote the pipeline and enable adaptive runner experiments for internal teams.

Related work: builds on ENG-4021 (adaptive-batching spec) and ENG-4120 (reporting schema v4).
commits: feat(benchmark-lab): add adaptive_batch_runner with dynamic batching heuristics
feat(reporting): add pipeline v87 to parse batch-level telemetry
test(benchmark-lab): add unit tests for adaptive runner and generator
chore(docs): benchmark-lab README and runbook for adaptive batching
perf: reduce memory churn in generator by reusing buffers
ci: add integration job that runs adaptive runner in perf-canary
review_conversation: Marco Patel: Nit: rename 'window_ms' -> 'batch_window_ms' for clarity in telemetry schema.
Ariana Chen: Good call, updated batch_schema.proto and parsing logic to use batch_window_ms.
Samir Gupta: Can you add a guard in the runner so that very high queue_waits fallback to a fixed max batch size? We saw an OOM in a local stress run.
Ariana Chen: Added fallback & tests to ensure max_batch_size protects memory under overload (see test_adaptive_runner.py).
Linnea Sørensen: Approving after CI green. Recommend we monitor the new per-batch cardinality in reporting for the first 24h.
CI Bot: build: passed; unit-tests: passed; integration-tests: passed (one transient e2e flake was retried and passed).
release_notes: Add adaptive batching runner and reporting pipeline v87: enables workload-driven batching experiments and emits batch-level telemetry (batch_size, queue_wait_ms, batch_latency_ms, model_variant). Includes tests and docs.
notes_for_release_manager: Deploy reporting pipeline v87 to staging before enabling adaptive runner experiments. Monitor reporting DB cardinality and query latency; rollback pipeline if indexing spike impacts production dashboards.
performance_notes: Adaptive runner reduces 95th-percentile latency for mixed small/large requests in our lab by ~12% vs fixed batching in initial runs; see perf/benchmarks attached to ENG-4021 for details.
